label: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
narrative: Gillibrand built the statutory machine that everything else in this domain hangs off. Section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA, P.L. 117-81, signed 27 December 2021 and codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373, ordered the Secretary of Defense and the DNI to stand up a permanent office to absorb the UAP Task Force, to force reporting into a centralized repository, and to report to Congress. It was restated a year later by Section 6802 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2023, enacted inside P.L. 117-263 on 23 December 2022, which named the office the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, put its Director reporting to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Principal Deputy DNI, and at subsection (j) demanded a written historical record report on the United States Government's dealings with UAP built from intelligence community records, oral history interviews and interviews of current and former officials. In February 2023 Gillibrand and Rubio led sixteen senators demanding full funding for AARO, arguing it 'provides the opportunity to integrate and resolve threats and hazards to the U.S., while also offering increased transparency.' She was an original cosponsor of S.Amdt. 797 in July 2023. Her posture is different from Schumer's: she legislates the plumbing, not the seizure. It is her plumbing — Sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA — that survived when Schumer's Review Board did not, and it is that surviving language she invoked on 8 May 2026 when the administration began releasing files, saying the government must 'finally meet its legal obligation to the American people.'
